title: Predictive headroom broker for micro-batch gating under bursty high-QPS
creator: Priya Rao
description: Build a predictive headroom broker that gates micro-batch admissions using short-term QPS forecasting, KV cache hotness projections, and GPU slab reclamation signals. The broker should provide soft backpressure decisions (defer, accept-small, accept-full, or route-to-fallback) with tenant-aware fairness and minimal P50 latency impact under bursty traffic patterns.
background: Current admission controller is reactive: it observes KV spill and GPU oom signals and then tightens micro-batch thresholds. Under multi-tenant bursty traffic we see oscillation and cascading tail latencies. Existing heuristics use fixed hysteresis windows which either waste GPU headroom or produce abrupt throttles. We need a proactive mechanism to smooth admissions by forecasting immediate demand and pre-emptively reclaiming low-value KV pages and shrinking continuous batch windows before an overload occurs.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight predictive broker process co-located with the admission controller. Key components: (1) 5s exponential smoothing QPS forecaster + percentile spike detector, (2) KV hotness short-term predictor (heat decay + recent access count), (3) a headroom model that maps forecasted tokens and KV footprint to estimated GPU slab usage, (4) policy layer that translates headroom delta into admission actions and per-tenant priorities. Policy supports soft actions: 'defer N ms', 'microbatch->min_tokens', 'evict-candidate-kv-pages', or 'route-to-low-cost-model'. The broker emits explainability tags for every decision to help observability and audits.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Forecast horizon too long -> inaccurate headroom, too short -> indistinguishable from reactive behavior.
- Aggressive pre-evictions risk quality regressions for in-flight sessions.
- Per-tenant fairness may reduce global throughput if strict isolation is enforced.
- Increased control-plane messages (broker -> serving runtime) could add CPU overhead; we prefer a compact protobuf with batch decision blobs.
experiments_and_results: Simulation (synthetic bursts): 10k req/s baseline with 5x 1s spikes. Predictive broker reduced tail (P99) latency by ~28% compared to hysteresis-only controller while keeping GPU utilization +4% on avg.

Canary on staging (region-us-west-2): enabled for 10 tenants for 24h. Observed fewer hard throttles and 12% lower KV spill events. Small increase in average token cost for two tenants due to pre-eviction overhead (~0.7%).
A/B feedback: latency improvement concentrated on short-context, low-batch requests. Large-context streaming sessions saw negligible difference because KV reuse dominates their cost profile.
implementation_notes:
- Broker will run as a sidecar in the batch admission pod.
- Use existing KV heatmap exporter as input (extend with 5s rolling counts).
- Decision proto: {timestamp, tenant_id, action, reason_code, predicted_headroom_delta, explain_tags}. Keep under 512 bytes per tenant per decision.
- Add opt-in feature flag: 'predictive_headroom_v1'.
- Fallback: if broker unavailable, admission controller reverts to current hysteresis policy.
rollout_plan:
Week 1: unit tests + simulation harness updates.
Feature flag gated code merged behind 'predictive_headroom_v1'.

Week 2: staging canary - 10 tenants (us-west-2). Monitor P50/P95/P99 latencies and KV spill rate.
Enable auto rollback trigger if P99 increases >10% or spike in OOMs.
Week 3: expand to 25% traffic for non-critical tenants, run for 72h. Collect cost delta and model quality signals.
Week 4: gradual ramp to 100% for selected shard-pools after review; full production rollout only after SRE signoff.
monitoring_and_metrics: Predicted headroom delta vs actual GPU slab delta (5s alignment)
Per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency, KV spill count, and GPU OOM count
Quality regressions: top-10 prompt eval accuracy drift for tenants with pre-evictions
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated and covered by unit + integration tests
Staging canary run with at least 48h of traffic showing no more than 5% increase in token cost for any tenant and P99 latency reduction >=10% for bursty workloads
SRE runbook updated with rollback triggers and broker healthchecks
Dashboard panels for the key metrics above and decision explainability logs available
Code reviewed and signed off by runtime and KV teams (PR links in links field)
